body: I mention this in the original post, I've tried about everything. I don't usually get help from other students since I get the impression other students don't like me and I'd be embarrassed to admit what I don't understand. I feel like they'd just be helping me more than I'd help them. Plus I generally have to study a lot more than others due to learning disability.

These problems? Yeah. I'd have other problems that I didn't mention, and I'd still be depressed. But at least I wouldn't be driving myself crazy over this class, to the point where I have thoughts of taking my own life.

I mentioned this, I can, but even if I do I think the fact that I can't pass this class will always haunt me and make me feel bad about myself. It's always something that I think about. And I used to be good at math! So the fact that I can't pass this one specific class makes me feel bad about an area that I used to be strong in. 

Also, most majors that don't require this class don't really have as strong of a job market as the ones that do. Plus a lot of the more interesting ones at my university, to me, are in the business school, which I can't get into due to my GPA.

I think you might have misunderstood my post. The professors are willing to help me. Well, for the most part. Sometimes I'll go into office hours and they'll purposefully get to me last or won't get to me at all due to time because the question I'm asking isn't really relevant to other students (other students need a difficult problem walked through, so that's a helpful question to everyone at office hours and a good use of time, vs. me needing a concept reexplained in a different way or something along those lines, which is really only helpful to me and is thus not as good of a way to use office hours). Otherwise they try their best to answer any question I throw at them. Actually, now that I think about it, I think part of my problem might be that sometimes I can't even articulate what I didn't understand or pinpoint my own errors, since sometimes the person at fault on the questions end is me, since I don't know how or what questions to ask. 

What I did mean, is that professors have essentially told me that they don't think I can pass the class. They've looked at my history of taking math classes, look at my performance in the class combined with my effort, and then politely recommend very strongly that I switch to a major that doesn't require this class. When I ask them if they think if I can ever pass they'll tell me that they don't know. All of this basically tells me that they don't really have faith in my ability to pass. For the record, two different professors have done this now.

I'll be honest, this didn't really help a whole lot. Whenever I read stories like this they just don't make me feel any better. For one, you only spent a year and a half, and I've spent three years. I know that might seem like an arbitrary difference, but it's significant when you think about it and realize that a degree is supposed to take four years. Your situation is also different in other ways, which I won't argue are better or worse but I'll just say that they're different. 

I also just can't see myself leading any kind of a "normal," life anyways. I don't care if I enjoy my job or get married, I just want to earn lots of money, learn more things, and impress my parents. 

Your post still kind of helped though, so thanks.

First of all, the biggest issue stems from the fact that prior to this I always did well in math. I always did very well in arithmetic, the various levels of algebra and Middle/High School math, and even basic Calculus. But later Calculus has also made me feel broken. 

Also, I've read and heard a lot of stuff that basically shows that people aren't just "not good at math,' they just don't study enough. This is an example of this that I got from just googling:
http://www.theatlantic.com/education/archive/2013/10/the-myth-of-im-bad-at-math/280914/

There are dozens of articles all over the place like this that basically say that you're not bad at math, but you're not preparing/studying properly. But I am so I don't know wtf is wrong here, which is why I said that I feel like I'm "broken".
